cite: US Department of Justice press release, 16 October 2019; BBC News, 16 October 2019 and 6 July 2020

fixes.d: A Korean-run darknet site that sold access to child sexual abuse videos for Bitcoin; it held over 250,000 unique videos and its server had more than one million Bitcoin addresses, one per account. IRS-CI tracing of Bitcoin transactions located the server in South Korea, and the operator, Son Jong-woo, was arrested on 5 March 2018. On 16 October 2019 the US DOJ announced 337 users arrested and charged, with leads sent to 38 countries (Korean police counted 310 arrests in 32 countries, 223 of them Koreans). He served 18 months in South Korea; on 6 July 2020 the Seoul High Court refused US extradition, and in July 2022 he received a further 24 months for concealing proceeds. DOJ said 45% of the videos analysed had not been known before.

note: DOJ release confirms 337 arrests/38 countries, 5 Mar 2018 arrest, 250,000 videos, 45% new. '1.2 million members, 4,000 paying' comes from Korean press via Wikipedia; DOJ only says >1m bitcoin addresses, so wording changed. BBC 6 Jul 2020 confirms extradition refusal; Reuters 5 Jul 2022 (via Wikipedia) for 24 months not opened. 310/32/223 Korean police figures via Wikipedia's Korean-press refs.

cite: US Department of Justice press release, 16 September 2021; BBC News, 5 August 2013; RTÉ, 20 March 2019

fixes.d: Freedom Hosting was a free anonymous dark web hosting service that ran from July 2008 to July 2013 and hosted over 200 child exploitation websites, including Lolita City, which Anonymous had attacked in 2011. The operator, Eric Eoin Marques, was arrested in Dublin in early August 2013 on a US warrant; the FBI accused him of being 'the largest facilitator of child porn on the planet'. After Ireland's Supreme Court dismissed his challenge in March 2019 he was extradited, pleaded guilty on 6 February 2020 to conspiracy to advertise child sexual abuse material, and on 16 September 2021 was sentenced to 27 years. DOJ said the sites held millions of images and videos, over 1.97 million not previously known to law enforcement.

note: Sentencing date was 16 September 2021, not 6 September. DOJ: service operated 24 Jul 2008-29 Jul 2013, >200 sites, plea 6 Feb 2020. BBC 2013 confirms Dublin arrest and FBI quote; RTÉ confirms Supreme Court dismissal 20 Mar 2019. Removed unverified details (Lolita City 1.4m images, OVH/MLAT).

cite: US Department of Justice press release, 8 January 2013; NBC News, 3 August 2011

fixes.d: An invitation-only bulletin board, used by an estimated 600 people, whose applicants had to upload abuse material of children aged 12 or under and keep uploading to stay. NBC reported the computers hosting the site were in Georgia, US, and the top administrators were in France and Canada. In August 2011 Attorney General Eric Holder and DHS Secretary Janet Napolitano announced charges against 72 people, with arrests on five continents including 43 in the US. By January 2013, 57 had been arrested, 45 had pleaded guilty and one was convicted at trial; 42 had been sentenced to between 10 years and life. Fifteen were known only by online identities. DOJ said at least 38 children were being abused by group members.

note: DOJ 2013 release: 72 charged, 57 arrested, 45 pleaded guilty (not 42), 42 sentenced 10 yrs-life, 15 known only by handles, 20 arrested abroad in 14 countries. NBC 2011: ~600 users, servers in Georgia (not Shreveport — Shreveport is where it was prosecuted), admins in France and Canada. '123 terabytes' not found in sources opened; removed.

cite: US Department of Justice press release, 17 December 2015; Wired, 'Operation Torpedo', 5 August 2014; Wired, 26 August 2014

fixes.d: Dutch police investigating Tor sites found one board's administrative account open and traced its server to Bellevue, Nebraska; the FBI identified Aaron McGrath, who hosted two sites at the server farm where he worked and a third at home. After a year of surveillance the FBI seized his servers in November 2012 and, under three search warrants, used a network investigative technique on the sites to reveal visitors' IP addresses. McGrath was sentenced to 20 years in January 2014. DOJ said in December 2015 that a New York man was the 19th person convicted in the investigation; one convicted user, Timothy DeFoggi, had been acting cybersecurity director at the US Department of Health and Human Services.

note: DOJ 17 Dec 2015 confirms McGrath 20 yrs, 19th conviction (so 18 besides operator is consistent). Wired confirms Dutch police lead, Bellevue NE, two sites at work/one at home, year of surveillance, Nov 2012 seizure. 'Operated sites for two weeks' not found in text opened; removed.

cite: VG (Norway), 'Breaking the dark net', 7 October 2017; US Department of Justice press release on Giftbox Exchange sentencing, August 2019

fixes.d: Childs Play launched on Tor on 15 April 2016 and, with over a million registered profiles, was described as the largest site of its kind. Its Canadian administrator, Benjamin Faulkner, was arrested in Virginia in early October 2016 with American Patrick Falte; in September 2017 a federal judge in Virginia sentenced both to life for sexually abusing a toddler, and in August 2019 both received 35 years for running a child exploitation enterprise on the related Giftbox Exchange site. Australia's Task Force Argos then ran Childs Play for 11 months, until September 2017, as part of Operation Artemis, to identify victims and offenders.

note: VG confirms launch 15 Apr 2016, >1m profiles, Argos ran it 11 months, closed Sept 2017, Operation Artemis, Virginia meeting Oct 2016. DOJ 2019 confirms life sentences (Sept 2017) and 35 years — the 35 years was for the Giftbox Exchange enterprise, not Childs Play. 'Canadian administrator sentenced to five years' not confirmed in sources opened; removed.
